subject: Post-call recap: ACME discovery — cost / TCO framing and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jared Miller <jared.miller@acmeexample.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 14:10:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: ACME discovery — cost / TCO framing and next steps

Hi Jared —

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and the cost/TCO levers we discussed so your finance/procurement folks have a clean summary. Please let me know if I mis-characterize anything.

Key pain points you shared
- High per-request inference spend (current vendor) and unpredictable monthly bills tied to burst traffic.
- Need for sub-300ms median latency for chat use cases across US regions.
- Security/compliance constraints for customer PII (require VPC + KMS).

Goals
- Move to a predictable monthly operating cost with a cap on tail spend.
- Hit latency SLOs for customer-facing chat and internal summarization jobs.
- Minimal engineering lift for migration (pilot on 1 product line).

Cost/TCO framing we covered
- Baseline estimate (no batching/caching): ~1.2M tokens/month -> estimated monthly token cost ~$30k at standard model price.
- With simple prefix caching (KV cache for system prompts + frequent prefixes) we expect ~30-40% token reduction -> ~$18k-$21k/month.
- With request-level batching during peak (continuous batching) and improved kernel selection for your 2k token average sequence, further 15-20% reduction -> ~$15k/month.
- Reserved Dedicated capacity option: reduces per-token unit cost and adds predictable monthly commitment. Example: 3x reserved nodes for expected peak gives ~25% lower unit cost on average vs hosted bursts (tradeoff: monthly commit).

Attachments: I attached a compact TCO workbook (ACME_TCO_v3.xlsx) with the assumptions above and a short Redwood pricing sheet. In the workbook I included 3 scenarios (baseline, caching+batching, reserved).

Proposed next steps
1) Share the attached TCO sheet with your finance/procurement and mark any assumptions that should be adjusted (token volumes, concurrency targets).
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive with your platform/infra team (30-45 min) to validate latency SLOs and discuss KV cache integration. Rafael can lead that.
3) If procurement wants pricing for a Dedicated commit vs hosted, we can provide a comparative quote and a 60-day pilot commitment.

Would Thursday or Friday next week work for the technical deep-dive?

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Exec, Enterprise | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0198
Redwood Inference

Marissa —

Appreciate the clear summary. A couple quick clarifications from our side before I forward to finance/procurement:
1) The baseline 1.2M tokens/month number — is that based on our estimate of 50k end-user chats/month with ~24 tokens per message + 6 system tokens? Can you include the per-conversation assumptions in the sheet?
2) For caching: when you say 30-40% reduction, does that assume a cold-start hit rate (i.e., initial prompt cached across sessions) or is that purely for repeated prefixes?
3) Procurement asked whether the Dedicated commit requires a 12-month minimum and what the early-termination terms look like.

Thursday afternoon should work for a tech deep-dive. Can you pencil in 11/26 3:00 PM EST (12:00 PM PST)? Rafael, can you join to cover integration questions?

Thanks,
Jared
Senior Product Manager — Messaging
ACME Corp

Thanks Jared — great questions. Short answers below and I updated the attached workbook to call out assumptions on the first tab.

1) Token assumptions: The 1.2M tokens/month baseline uses your estimate of ~50k end-user chats/month, average 24 tokens per user message + 6 system tokens and ~1.2 assistant turns per chat on average. I put a per-conversation breakdown in the workbook so you can change the numbers.

2) Caching assumptions: The 30-40% reduction modeled is primarily for repeated prefixes + shared system prompts across sessions. We modeled a conservative cold-start hit rate (20% initial reuse) and increasing hit rate over time as session patterns stabilize. I added a sensitivity table in the workbook showing hit rates from 10-60%.

3) Dedicated terms: Standard Dedicated contracts are 12-month minimum. For pilots we can offer a 60-day pilot under a limited commit with a ramp schedule; early termination terms are negotiable for enterprise (we typically pro-rate remaining committed funds with a limited fee). I'll introduce Procurement to our finance team if you want formal language.

I've attached the updated ACME_TCO_v3.xlsx (v3) with the assumption tab. Also attaching redwood_pricing_sheet.pdf with short descriptions of Hosted vs Dedicated pricing.

Proposed: Tech deep-dive Thu 11/26 3:00 PM EST works for us — Rafael will join. I'll send a calendar invite shortly.

Best,
Marissa
